summary: POC scoping focused on commercial guardrails for a 6-week pilot: success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds), workload sizing and benchmark plan, pilot credits (~$25k) and limits, timeline for runs and procurement path to enterprise contract.
transcript: 00:00 Aaron (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick roundtable — i'm Aaron Chen, AE for Redwood. with me is Samir, our se. 00:08 Maya: thanks Aaron, Maya here (Head of ML at Sunburst). Ethan and Priya are on, Kyle from security as well. 00:15 Aaron: awesome. objective today is to align on POC success criteria, how big the workload is, what benchmarks we run, and the commercial guardrails — credits, pilot terms, procurement path. feel free to interrupt. 00:30 Samir (Redwood SE): i'll start with a quick framing of what a typical pilot looks like from our side — usually 4-8 weeks, we provide eval credits, and we run benchmark harnesses for latency, throughput, and quality compared to baselines. 00:45 Ethan: 4-8 weeks is fine. our main must-haves are sub-200ms median latency for single-turn generation on our trimmed prompts and p95 under 600ms, and must not degrade classification accuracy more than 1.5% on our eval set. 01:05 Maya: yep and to add — our workloads are a mix: 60% short-fill clinical-note generation (avg 120 tokens), 30% summarization (avg 280 tokens), 10% complex question answering that hits longer context (up to 2k tokens). we can share sample prompts. 01:24 Samir: good, that mix helps a lot. for capacity sizing we need expected RPS and concurrency. Ethan, what are you seeing in peak? 01:32 Ethan: peak is around 35 qps for the summarization service during batch hours; typical steady state is 6-8 qps, spike concurrency up to 20 simultaneous sessions for long-context QA. 01:45 Aaron: so for the pilot we will size to emulate peak traffic — suggest we provision for a sustained 40 rps headroom and test bursts to 80 to validate autoscaling and fallbacks. does that sound right? 01:56 Maya: yes, and we want to test fallback behavior to a smaller quantized variant (if latency or cost exceeds thresholds). 02:05 Samir: we'll include a model variant plan in the benchmark — hosted open model vs quantized private variant. for benchmarks we'll measure median, p95, p99 latency, token cost, throughput, and a quality delta against your golden eval set. 02:18 Alex (Data Analyst): for the quality measurement, we prefer a set of 500 labelled examples per task; is that enough? 02:25 Samir: that should be fine to get a stable signal for relative regression detection. we'll note statistical variance. 02:32 Aaron: commercial guardrails — to surface our standard POC offer: we typically provide a pilot credit pool, for this scale we recommend 25k USD in credits covering hosted inference and benchmark runs. credits are one-time, expire at end of pilot, and overages are billable. 02:48 Priya (Procurement): can you clarify what the credits cover? do we need an SOW or PO before you provision? 02:55 Aaron: credits cover token charges for hosted API, and limited support hours for integration and benchmark assistance. we can provision pilot access on a simple SOW or pilot letter of intent — no full enterprise contract required to start. we do ask for an MSA/TPA for enterprises if the pilot uses dedicated or private deployment. 03:13 Priya: procurement typically needs price caps and a PO for credits. will you accept a PO against the pilot SOW? 03:20 Aaron: yes we accept PO. often customers issue PO for the value of credits; we can also accommodate a supplier invoice model. 03:27 Kyle (Security): security questions — will data from these benchmarks be retained? what about logs, SSO, KMS? 03:35 Samir: good q. for hosted pilots we retain logs for 30 days by default, can change per agreement. we support SSO/SAML and integration with customer KMS for dedicated/private. for hosted we don't hold customer keys but we can discuss encryption at rest and in flight. we'll share our security pack. 03:52 Kyle: please also include SOC2 attestation and any ISO/PCI docs you have. 03:56 Aaron: will do, i'll attach the security binder. 04:00 Maya: timeline — we'd like the pilot to start first week of June and run 6 weeks. we want one initial benchmark in week 1, performance tuning in week 2-3, then a final acceptance run in week 6. 04:12 Aaron: that timeline is doable. proposed schedule: week 0 (kickoff & access), week 1 run baseline benchmarks, week 2 tuning & config changes, week 3 scale tests, week 4-5 regression monitoring, week 6 final acceptance + go/no-go. 04:26 Ethan: for acceptance criteria — we will require: median latency <200ms for short prompts, p95 <600ms for mixed workload, quality deltas <=1.5% vs our baseline, and cost per 1k tokens <= our internal benchmark (Samir we'll share). 04:42 Samir: we'll capture those as test cases. also note that caching and batching behavior can change results; we'll use a deterministic harness to make results repeatable. 04:52 Aaron: procurement/contracting path — after pilot acceptance the normal path is: we hand over the usage reports and SOW -> procurement issues PO for committed reserved capacity or transitions to monthly billing -> sign enterprise contract (MSA + SOW). if dedicated/private required, there will be additional procurement for infra and an onboarding SOW. 05:12 Priya: how often do customers convert after a pilot? we need references for typical pricing. 05:18 Aaron: typical conversion rates are high when success criteria met — many convert to reserved capacity with a 6-12 month commit. i'll share anonymized case studies and a pricing sheet. 05:28 Maya: about model variants — we might need an on-prem quantized variant for PHI-sensitive flows. what is the path to an air-gapped/private deployment? 05:36 Samir: we can do a Private deployment, it's a heavier lift: site prep, networking, KMS integration, and a separate license. timeline is usually 8-12 weeks after SOW. for the pilot we can emulate private performance with quantized model hosted in our dedicated pool and provide guarantees for comparison. 05:52 Alex: are there limits on the pilot credits? what if we overshoot during scale tests? 05:58 Aaron: credits are a soft limit; we notify at thresholds (50/75/90%) and overages auto-bill unless agreed otherwise. we can set hard caps if procurement requires. 06:08 Priya: need invoice line items split for credits vs support and potential dedicated infra. 06:14 Aaron: we'll provide a pilot pricing attachment showing credits, support hours, and optional dedicated pricing. 06:21 Maya: acceptance run — what does your report include? raw traces, latency distribution, cost breakdown, and quality metrics? 06:28 Samir: yes — we'll provide a benchmark report with p50/p95/p99, token counts, per-route cost, and model delta charts. we'll also include request traces for problematic cases. 06:39 Ethan: do you offer SLA for pilot? 06:43 Aaron: pilots don't carry full SLA; we do ensure prioritized support. SLA is linked to Dedicated/Enterprise contracts post-conversion. 06:51 Maya: okay, one more - are there restrictions on training/fine-tuning? we only want inference in this pilot. 06:57 Samir: pilot will be inference-only and we will not persist customer training artifacts. 07:02 Aaron: great. quick recap and next steps: Aaron to send pilot terms and draft SOW with 25k credits; Samir to upload benchmark harness and example prompts; Sunburst to share 500 labeled eval samples and redacted workload; Kyle to confirm security contacts and required attestations; Priya to confirm PO and procurement timeline. 07:22 Priya: we'll try to turn PO in the week after SOW. 07:26 Aaron: any other blockers? 07:27 Maya: none from me. 07:28 Ethan: no. ok thanks everyone. 07:30 Aaron: thanks, we'll follow up with deck + security binder + benchmark template. link to shared spreadsheet: https://tiny.redwood/pilot-spreadsheet (note: placeholder).
